source.title: Emergence and Evolution of Interpretable Concepts in Diffusion Models
source.authors: Berk Tınaz; Zalan Fabian; M. Soltanolkotabi

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper invokes the superposition hypothesis as motivation for using SAEs, then uses SAE features to study diffusion representations. It does not test whether sparse features overlap to represent more features than dimensions, or the other listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE-based segmentation, temporal feature metrics, and image-editing results. The temporal concept-cohesion and concept-separability metrics are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version; they measure Word2Vec similarity among dictionary labels, not superposition geometry or feature-unit completeness. Segmentation and intervention results are not rows because they measure image prediction or editing rather than a listed claim version.
record.test_reason: The paper assumes superposition to justify expansive TopK SAEs on Stable Diffusion v1.4 activations. It then uses SAE concepts for layout prediction and editing. It reports no test of overlapping directions, capacity competition, polysemanticity origins, feature completeness or canonicity, or feature dimensionality. V4 names LLMs, and this is a diffusion U-Net. The SAE reconstruction metrics in Table 1 are training diagnostics, not a test of sparse-feature recovery.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. Coarse layout is predictable from SAE features at the first step and largely finalized by mid-trajectory. SAE-concept interventions control composition early (80% spatial success at t=1.0) and style mid-trajectory (93% global edit success at t=0.5). Superposition is assumed, not tested.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses TopK SAEs on Stable Diffusion activations to identify and intervene on image concepts; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported dictionary cohesion and separability metrics vary across diffusion timesteps.

fits_no_version.finding: Word2Vec-based cohesion of SAE concept-dictionary labels rises from 0.588 (t=1.0) to 0.664 (t=0.0). Separability similarity falls from 0.433 to 0.344.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In SD v1.4, SAE concepts become semantically purer and more distinct over the course of reverse diffusion.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix D/G report redundant concepts firing on the same regions, plus context-free positional concepts the authors attribute to SAE optimization artifacts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE dictionaries on diffusion activations contain duplicate and artifact features (qualitative only).

record.problems: The study focuses on one diffusion model. It trains separate SAEs for different timesteps, so features across timesteps are not directly comparable. The cohesion and separability metrics concern Word2Vec embeddings of dictionary labels rather than model-feature geometry. The authors also note annotation limitations and U-Net skip-connection leakage for interventions.
record.rows_left_out: Segmentation-prediction results (Section 4.2, Figure 3 and Appendix C) and image-intervention results (Section 4.3, Figures 4–6 and Appendix E.2, Tables 4–5) were left out because they measure image layout prediction or editing effects, not a listed claim version.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, no sparsity transition, no geometry of feature directions.
All: no capacity or importance analysis.
Not tested in LLMs. SAE explained variance on SD v1.4 (36–78%, Table 1) is reported only as training metrics.
No test of completeness, stability across seeds, or canonicity. Separate SAEs per timestep are not compared.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. The qualitative observations on redundant and context-free features loosely relate to V5 but are not tested claims about canonicity, so no verdict is given.

versions.untested_parts: No test of sparse features outnumbering dimensions, overlapping or near-orthogonal directions, a sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometry.
No test of capacity competition, dedicated dimensions for important features, or feature sharing due to limited capacity.
No test of whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.
The study examines Stable Diffusion v1.4, not LLMs; it does not test feature spreading across neurons or SAE recovery in LLMs.
No test of whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of the model representation.
No comparison of one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Stable Diffusion v1.4 (SDv1.4)
rows.operation_detail: Measured concept cohesion as average cosine distance of dictionary-item Word2Vec embeddings from their concept center.
rows.note: Aggregate across concepts; this measures dictionary-label embedding cohesion, not geometric overlap among model features.

relation.reason: Section 2 explicitly assumes superposition, and Section 3.1 uses it to justify expansive SAE encodings; results concern the resulting method and diffusion dynamics.

tranche.reason: Uses TopK SAEs for diffusion-concept interpretation, layout prediction and editing. The reported Word2Vec metrics do not test any listed superposition version.

source_check.notes: The source defines cohesion using cosine distance but interprets increasing scores as greater purity, an internal inconsistency faithfully reflected by the rows. Both metrics concern Word2Vec label embeddings, not model-feature geometry.
